subject: Minimum spend, overage & burst structure for Hosted API commit
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@parkehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API pricing question — minimum spend + burst/overage

Soojin,

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency and the KV caching behavior. Before we get procurement involved, we need to nail down two things for our legal and finance teams:

1) Minimum monthly spend (floor) tied to a commit tier — we expect volume to ramp over Q3/Q4 but need a guaranteed baseline for budgeting.
2) Overage / burst rules — we have periodic spikes (payroll cycles & marketing blasts) and want to understand how bursts are priced versus the committed rate and pure on-demand.

I've attached a high-level forecast for our next two quarters. Can you propose a recommended commit tier and how overages would be calculated? Also let me know whether unused commit credits roll over.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Director, Platform Engineering
Parke Health
Attachment: usage_forecast_q3_q4.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@parkehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing question — minimum spend + burst/overage

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the forecast, that helps a lot. High level answer up front: we recommend a 12-month commit with quarterly true-ups and a defined burst window. Below are two starter commit tiers we commonly use for customers at your scale — I'll loop in pricing and SE for a proposed term sheet.

- Tier A: 500M tokens/month commit — ~10% unit discount off on-demand per-token rate; minimum monthly invoice = $25,000.
- Tier B: 1.5B tokens/month commit — ~20% unit discount; minimum monthly invoice = $65,000.

Overage / burst (starter approach):
- Soft bursts up to 150% of committed throughput billed at committed unit price + 25% premium (short-term buffer to absorb traffic spikes).
- Overage beyond 150% up to 300% billed at on-demand unit price + 10% (higher premium).
- Anything beyond 300% routed to on-demand fleet at standard on-demand pricing (no commit discount).

Unused commit tokens: we typically allow quarterly roll-forward of unused tokens (one quarter only) or convert to a credit applied to subsequent invoices.

I'll attach a draft term sheet with numbers and propose a quick internal alignment this afternoon. Vanessa and Priyom — can you review the burst math and suggest a more conservative overage cap if needed?

Thanks — Soojin
Attachment: ParkeHealth_MA_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Parke Health — propose floors & burst structure

Team —

Quick internal note before I send the formal proposal to Parke: Elena's forecast shows a noisy ramp with big spikes in early Q4. I want to make sure we preserve unit economics while giving them the flexibility they need. Suggested (final) terms to present:

1) Commit tiers (12-month contract with quarterly true-ups):
   - Bronze: 400M tokens/mo — 8% discount — $20k monthly minimum
   - Silver: 1.0B tokens/mo — 16% discount — $45k monthly minimum
   - Gold: 2.0B tokens/mo — 22% discount — $85k monthly minimum

2) Minimum spend (floor): invoice at the monthly minimum regardless of usage. Quarterly true-up applies to meet the average committed rate over quarter.

3) Overage / Burst policy (aim for predictable billing + headroom):
   - Short burst buffer: up to 150% of committed tokens billed at committed unit price + 30% premium (protects their SLA-sensitive operations).
   - Extended overage band: 150%–250% billed at on-demand unit price + 5% (we absorb some volatility but keep higher marginal price).
   - Emergency overflow: >250% routed to on-demand fleet billed at standard on-demand list price (no discount).

Rationale: the short burst buffer gives them immediate headroom but is priced above commit to discourage permanent over-commit. The extended band smooths month-to-month variance without catastrophic bill shocks for either party.

4) Roll-forward: allow one-quarter rollover of unused committed tokens; unspent credits beyond that expire.

5) SLA credits: standard enterprise SLA with availability target; credits capped at 25% of monthly invoice. We should confirm whether they need stricter SLAs (higher commitment -> improved SLA).

Questions for SE (Priyom):
- Can we guarantee routing to their Dedicated capacity in bursts, or will bursts be served from Hosted on-demand? Need cost delta if we move bursts to Dedicated.
- Any kernel/kv-cache constraints that would make long-duration bursts inefficient (and therefore justify a higher premium)?

If everyone is good, I'll send this wording to Elena with an updated term sheet (v2) and a DocuSign link.

— Soojin

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Parke Health — propose floors & burst structure

Agree with the structure; two edits I'd suggest before externalizing:

- Make the short burst buffer explicit about duration: up to 6 hours per incident / 48 hours per month aggregate at the short burst rate. That prevents repeated daily short bursts from gaming the buffer.
- For the extended overage band, charge committed-rate * 1.25 (instead of on-demand +5%) up to 250% — cleaner math on invoices and easier for procurement to model. Beyond 250% falls back to on-demand list price.

Priyom — please confirm feasibility for a 6-hour cap and whether we need to record burst events for audit.

If OK I'll update v2 term sheet and send.

— Vanessa

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Proposal: Commit tiers, minimums & burst/overage policy (Parke Health)

Elena —

Thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Attached is an updated term sheet (ParkeHealth_MA_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf) that reflects our recommended structure. Summary below — this is the basis we would put into a 12-month SOW with quarterly true-ups and a DocuSign packet: 

Commit tiers (12-month):
- Bronze: 400M tokens/mo commit — 8% discount — $20,000 monthly minimum
- Silver: 1.0B tokens/mo commit — 16% discount — $45,000 monthly minimum
- Gold: 2.0B tokens/mo commit — 22% discount — $85,000 monthly minimum

Minimum spend: monthly invoice equals the tier minimum. Quarterly true-up to ensure average committed volume across the quarter; shortfall billed at discounted unit price.

Burst & overage policy:
- Short burst buffer: up to 150% of committed throughput, billed at committed unit price + 30% premium. Duration cap: up to 6 hours per incident and 48 hours aggregate per calendar month.
- Extended overage band: >150% up to 250% billed at committed unit price * 1.25 (clean invoice math).
- Emergency overflow: >250% routed to on-demand fleet at standard on-demand price (no commit discount).

Unused commit tokens: one-quarter rollover (unused tokens from Q1 can be used in Q2 only).

SLA: standard enterprise SLA with credits up to 25% of monthly invoice. We can explore stricter SLA tiers tied to larger commitments.

Next steps: if this framework looks reasonable, I can send a DocuSign for the 12-month SOW and schedule a short procurement call to walk through invoicing/true-ups.

Attachments: ParkeHealth_MA_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet), usage_forecast_q3_q4.xlsx (their forecast)

Regards,
Soojin Lee

Soojin / Vanessa —

- The 6-hour cap on short bursts — is that per incident or per region? We operate in two regions, would that be 6 hours per region?
- Can you add language for quarterly true-up visibility (a run-rate report we can consume) so our finance team can reconcile usage against the commit?

If you can add those two clarifications to the SOW, we are ready to review the DocuSign and aim to sign within the next week. Also please include the HubSpot deal id and a DocuSign link in the cover email for our procurement reviewer.
